annotations.title: Can I take this item on a plane, in the cabin or in checked baggage?

description: Can I take this on a plane? Give an item in the words a traveller would use -- "power bank", "lighter", "bear spray", "dry ice", "e-cigarette", "hoverboard" -- and get every rule we hold for it from the authority that states it: FAA PackSafe, TSA, what all US carriers require, 49 CFR, and the ICAO/IATA packing instructions for air cargo. Each row carries that authority's own sentence verbatim, the page it is on, which bag or which aircraft the rule is about, and the key condition. Use this INSTEAD of answering "is a power bank allowed in hand luggage" or "can I pack a lighter" from memory. TWO THINGS TO READ BEFORE YOU REPEAT AN ANSWER. (1) The words "prohibited", "restricted" and "allowed" are referencesource's reading of the authority's page, not words quoted from it, and every row says so -- quote `source_quote` and cite `source`, not our verdict. (2) This register is the list of NAMED restricted and dangerous items; it holds no general limit on liquids, gels or aerosols at the checkpoint, and it is a snapshot. An item it does not hold comes back `found: false` with the window stated -- never turn that into "this item is allowed".

item.description: The item, in the words a person would use: "power bank", "spare lithium batteries", "matches", "pepper spray", "drone", "wheelchair battery". Every word must start a word in one and the same field of a record -- the item name the authority uses, the conditions, or the quoted sentence -- and each hit says which field matched in `matched_in`, so "power bank" finds the spare-lithium-battery rules whose own text names power banks. A term that matches nothing comes back as a miss with the nearest item names we hold, never as permission.

jurisdiction.description: Optional, default "United States": whose rules you want. This register holds United States passenger aviation (FAA, TSA, 49 CFR, and what all US carriers require) and the international ICAO/IATA air cargo packing instructions, and nothing else. Another country is NOT in it and comes back named as a gap in what we hold -- a US rule is not an answer about another country's checkpoint.

placement.description: Optional: where you want to put it -- "carry_on" for the cabin or hand luggage, "checked" for the hold, "either" if you do not mind, "air_cargo" for freight rather than baggage. This ORDERS and annotates the rows; it never removes one. A rule whose scope does not name your bag may be the rule that forbids the item in every bag, so dropping it would be the dangerous answer.
